name: David Schweikert

accounts.evidence: His campaign site, which now promotes his run for Arizona governor, links to https://twitter.com/DavidSchweikert.

notes: The site's YouTube link is 'davidschweikertforgovernor', so this account is now used for the governor campaign. It is under his personal name, so it could also be called personal.

name: Elijah Crane

accounts.evidence: A 2022 Cronkite News candidate profile of Eli Crane embeds a post attributed to 'Eli Crane (@EliCrane_CEO)'.

notes: The evidence is from 2022, and I did not check whether the account is still active or renamed. The campaign site eliforarizona.com returned HTTP 403, so I could not check its X link. Unconfirmed lead: a search summary said ProPublica's Politwoops listed 'EliCraneAZ' as one of his accounts, but the Politwoops page I opened no longer lists accounts.

name: Greg Stanton

accounts.evidence: The 'Greg Stanton for Congress' site (footer 'Paid for by Greg Stanton for Congress') links to https://www.x.com/gregstantonaz.
His LegiStorm profile lists https://x.com/MayorStanton as an X account for him, next to the official RepGregStanton.

notes: MayorStanton is probably his older account from when he was mayor of Phoenix. LegiStorm does not label it as official or campaign, and I did not check whether it is still active.

name: Andy Biggs

notes: This is his 2026 Arizona governor campaign account. I did not look for any earlier congressional campaign account (biggsforcongress.com).

name: Kevin Kiley
notes: His campaign site, electkevinkiley.com ('Paid for by Kevin Kiley for Congress', which Wikipedia lists as his campaign website), shows no X, Facebook or Instagram links in the text I fetched. LegiStorm lists only the official RepKiley. kevinkiley.com is a domain for sale, not his site. No personal or campaign X account was found.
